summary.name: DockLift
summary.one_liner: DockLift is a macOS menu bar utility that moves an app's window to the screen you are using when you click its Dock icon, for multi-display setups.
use_cases: Bring an app window back from a second display when clicking its Dock icon
Gather an app's windows from other displays onto the current screen with Shift-click
Restore minimized windows from the Dock on a multi-monitor Mac
Stop Dock clicks from opening windows on an off-screen display
summary.what_it_does: DockLift runs in the macOS menu bar. When you click an app's Dock icon, it moves that app's recent window to the screen you are currently using and brings it to the front. Holding Shift while clicking a Dock icon moves that app's windows from other displays to the current screen. It also works when the app is already open on another display and restores minimized windows. A simple menu bar control turns it on or off, and specific apps can be ignored. It is installed via Homebrew cask and needs macOS Accessibility permission to move windows.
notable: Shift-click Dock icon gathers an app's windows from other displays
Lives in the menu bar with on/off toggle
caveats: Requires macOS Accessibility permission to move windows
Moves the app's recent window, not necessarily all windows (except with Shift-click)
